(CNN)  -- Darren Tuck, the man who gave police a tape depicting the rape of a 3-year-old girl, turned himself in Sunday to Nye County, Nevada, authorities. Darren Tuck turned himself in to authorities Sunday. He earlier gave police the tape of the girl. Tuck had recently given police the videotape, saying he found it in the desert, Sheriff Tony De Meo said. Police said he had the tape for at least five months before turning it in. He was being sought on a parole violation for failure to pay child support, but police -- who have said they want to question him further -- had been unable to locate him. Tuck, of Nevada, allegedly showed the tape to others, and faces between 10 years to life in prison for exhibiting pornography and one to six years for possession of child pornography, said De Meo. Tuck's attorney Harry Kuehn said last week on CNN's "Nancy Grace" that Tuck had been "wracked by indecision" as to what to do with the tape once he realized what it was. "You have to consider what kind of concerns my client had," the attorney said. "He's previously dealt with the sheriff's office in Nye County; it was previously unsatisfactory." The four-year-old videotape shows the 3-year-old girl being raped in Las Vegas, Nevada. Last week, she was found safe. Now seven, the girl was found Friday with family in Las Vegas after thousands of tips poured in to police, thanks to an appeal by police to the news media to show the girl's picture. CNN and other news organizations did so until the child was found, and De Meo asked media to stop showing the picture. "The mother has cooperated with us," De Meo said. "We believe that the mother was not aware of anything that went on with this young girl. It was very sad for her to find this out." Authorities have identified Chester A. Stiles, 37, as the suspect in the tape. A  resident of Pahrump, Nevada, he remains at-large, De Meo said. Pahrump is about 60 miles west of Las Vegas. Stiles was a distant friend of the girl's family, De Meo said. Someone close to Stiles told investigators Stiles is a "survivalist type" and always carries a weapon, Nye County District Attorney Bob Beckett said. Todd Allen, a Las Vegas resident, told CNN he once lived with the girl from the video and her mother. He said he recognizes his old apartment from scenes in the video. He said he knows the suspect because Allen's mother dated Stiles and the couple spent time together at Allen's apartment.  Watch Allen describe Stiles and the girl » . Allen said nobody realized the child had been abused. "She's what you'd expect a little girl in elementary school to be like," he said. "You would never know something like that happened. Ever." Allen said he never witnessed Stiles physically assault anyone. "But I have seen him verbally and mentally assault many people," Allen told CNN. "He's good with mind games. He's good at twisting people's realities and manipulating people." De Meo addressed Stiles directly on Saturday: "Turn yourself in to your local law enforcement agency," he said. "Understand this: Law enforcement not only has a long arm, but a long memory. You will not be forgotten by members of this agency or any other law enforcement agency." The FBI is also seeking Stiles on state charges of sexual assault and lewdness with a minor under the age of 14 in a separate matter, De Meo said.  E-mail to a friend .

outputs.L1:
**(CNN) —** Darren Tuck, the man who gave police a videotape depicting the rape of a 3-year-old girl, turned himself in to authorities in Nye County, Nevada, on Sunday.

Tuck recently gave the tape to police, saying he had found it in the desert, Sheriff Tony De Meo said. However, police said Tuck had possessed the tape for at least five months before handing it over.

Authorities had been seeking Tuck for a parole violation stemming from his failure to pay child support. Police, who have said they want to question him further, had previously been unable to locate him.

Tuck, a Nevada resident, allegedly showed the tape to others. He faces 10 years to life in prison for exhibiting pornography and one to six years for possession of child pornography, De Meo said.

Tuck’s attorney, Harry Kuehn, said last week on CNN’s “Nancy Grace” that his client had been “wracked by indecision” over what to do with the tape once he realized what it contained.

“You have to consider what kind of concerns my client had,” Kuehn said. “He’s previously dealt with the sheriff’s office in Nye County; it was previously unsatisfactory.”

The four-year-old videotape shows the girl, then 3, being raped in Las Vegas, Nevada. She was found safe last week.

Now 7, the girl was located with family members in Las Vegas on Friday after police received thousands of tips. The tips followed an appeal by authorities asking news organizations to show the girl’s picture. CNN and other media outlets did so until the child was found, after which De Meo asked them to stop displaying the image.

“The mother has cooperated with us,” De Meo said. “We believe that the mother was not aware of anything that went on with this young girl. It was very sad for her to find this out.”

Authorities have identified Chester A. Stiles, 37, as the suspect shown in the tape. Stiles, a resident of Pahrump, Nevada, remains at large, De Meo said. Pahrump is about 60 miles west of Las Vegas.

De Meo said Stiles was a distant friend of the girl’s family. Someone close to Stiles told investigators that he is a “survivalist type” who always carries a weapon, according to Nye County District Attorney Bob Beckett.

Las Vegas resident Todd Allen told CNN that he once lived with the girl shown in the video and her mother. He said he recognized his former apartment in scenes from the recording.

Allen also said he knows the suspect because his mother dated Stiles, and the couple spent time together at Allen’s apartment.

**Watch Allen describe Stiles and the girl »**

Allen said no one realized the child had been abused.

“She’s what you’d expect a little girl in elementary school to be like,” he said. “You would never know something like that happened. Ever.”

Allen said he never saw Stiles physically assault anyone.

“But I have seen him verbally and mentally assault many people,” Allen told CNN. “He’s good with mind games. He’s good at twisting people’s realities and manipulating people.”

On Saturday, De Meo addressed Stiles directly.

“Turn yourself in to your local law enforcement agency,” he said. “Understand this: Law enforcement not only has a long arm, but a long memory. You will not be forgotten by members of this agency or any other law enforcement agency.”

The FBI is also seeking Stiles on state charges of sexual assault and lewdness with a minor under the age of 14 in a separate case, De Meo said.

# Girl in Four-Year-Old Abuse Tape Found Alive and Safe; Police Identify Suspect

**LAS VEGAS —** Authorities investigating a videotaped sexual assault of a young child announced a major breakthrough Tuesday, saying the girl depicted in the recording has been identified and is alive and safe. Police also identified **Chester Stiles** as the man shown in the tape, while **Darren Tuck**, the man connected to the recording’s discovery, remains in custody over a parole violation and faces charges involving the possession and exhibition of illegal material.

Investigators said the tape was recorded approximately four years before it came to law enforcement’s attention. The girl was about 3 years old at the time and is now around 7, according to authorities. Police emphasized that she is no longer in danger and is being protected, withholding her name and other identifying information because she is a minor and the victim of sexual abuse.

The child’s identification followed an intensive public appeal after investigators released images of the suspected assailant while carefully concealing the victim’s identity. Tips from the public helped detectives identify the man as Stiles, who was described as having had access to the girl when the recording was made.

Authorities did not disclose the child’s present location or provide details about her family, citing her privacy and the continuing criminal investigation.

## Stiles identified as man in recording

Police said Stiles is the individual depicted abusing the child in the tape. Investigators were working to locate him and determine whether he may have had access to other children.

The identification marked a critical development in a case that had drawn widespread attention because investigators initially did not know either the suspect’s name or whether the child had survived and reached safety.

Officials said the recording appeared to document multiple acts of abuse. They declined to describe its contents in detail, saying such information could further traumatize the victim and interfere with any eventual prosecution.

## Tuck held on parole violation

Tuck, who came into possession of the tape before it reached police, was taken into custody for allegedly violating the terms of his parole. Authorities said he also faces charges related to **possessing and exhibiting illegal obscene material involving a child**.

Investigators allege Tuck did not immediately turn the recording over to police and instead showed it to other people. Under child-exploitation laws, possessing, copying, distributing or displaying such material can constitute separate criminal conduct, even when the person in possession did not create the original recording.

Police were examining how Tuck obtained the tape, how long he had it and whether copies were made or circulated. Detectives were also seeking to identify everyone who may have viewed or handled it before law enforcement took custody of the evidence.

The allegations against Tuck are separate from the assault shown in the recording. Authorities have not accused him of being the man depicted abusing the girl. His custody stems from the parole matter and the alleged possession and exhibition of the material.

## Investigation remains active

The discovery that the girl is alive and safe resolved the most urgent question facing investigators, but police said the case remains active. Detectives are continuing to establish when and where the recording was made, how it changed hands and whether additional evidence or victims exist.

Authorities urged anyone with information about Stiles, his whereabouts or his past contact with children to contact law enforcement. They also warned members of the public not to seek out, copy or share the recording, noting that every reproduction further exploits the child and may violate criminal law.

Officials said the girl and her family are being offered appropriate support services. They asked news organizations and the public to avoid speculation or the disclosure of details that could lead to her identification.

The identification of both the child and the suspected assailant gives prosecutors a clearer path toward building a case, but any charges against Stiles would remain allegations unless and until proven in court.
